item.title: Song Eon-seok: "Constitutional amendment is an attempt by the Democratic Party to frame the People Power Party as 'pro-martial law' to gain an advantage in local elections" (송언석 “개헌, 국힘에 ‘계엄 옹호’ 프레임 씌워 지선 유리한 고지 점하려는 저의”)
item.description:
Song Eon-seok, the floor leader of the People Power Party (PPP), said on the 8th, "A constitutional amendment requires consensus between the ruling and opposition parties," refuting claims by National Assembly Speaker Woo Won-shik and the Democratic Party of Korea that the PPP was responsible for the failure to pass the constitutional amendment. (송언석 국민의힘 원내대표는 8일 “개헌은 여야 합의가 필수”라며 헌법개정안 처리가 무산이 국민의힘 때문이라는 우원식 국회의장과 더불어민주당의 주장을 반박했다.)

Floor Leader Song met with reporters immediately after the plenary session adjourned at the National Assembly's Rotunda Hall and stated, "The very act of proposing (the constitutional amendment) that was rejected (the previous day) violates the principle of 'one subject, one session,' which prohibits reintroducing a rejected bill in the same session." He added, "The Speaker unilaterally convened the plenary session without agreement between the negotiating groups in a clearly unconstitutional act, leaving our party with no choice but to respond with a filibuster." (송 원내대표는 이날 국회 로텐더홀에서 본회의 산회 직후 기자들과 만나 “(전날) 부결된 (헌법 개정안을) 상정한다는 거 자체가 한번 부결된 건을 동일 회기에 다시 상정하지 못하도록 하는 일사부재의 원칙에 어긋난다”며 “명백히 위헌인 행위를 국회의장이 교섭단체간 합의도 없이 일방적으로 (본회의를) 개최해 우리 당은 할 수 없이 필리버스터로 대응할 수밖에 없던 상태였다”고 밝혔다.)

After Speaker Woo announced at that day's plenary session that he would propose the constitutional amendment and 50 bills, the PPP declared it would counter all bills with filibusters. In response, Speaker Woo criticized the PPP, saying, "I will not propose the constitutional amendment. I cannot but express strong regret toward the PPP, which has scuttled a constitutional amendment for the first time in 39 years." Regarding Floor Leader Song's claim of a violation of the principle of 'one subject, one session,' the Speaker's office maintained that since the constitutional amendment proposed the previous day failed to meet the voting quorum (approval by two-thirds of sitting members), the vote was not valid, and there is no issue with a re-vote. (우 의장이 이날 국회 본회의에서 헌법개정안(개헌안)과 법안 50건을 상정하겠다고 밝히자 국민의힘은 모든 법안 필리버스터(무제한 토론)으로 맞서겠다고 나섰다. 이에 우 의장은 “헌법 개정안을 상정하지 않겠다. 39년 만에 개헌을 무산시킨 국민의힘에 강력한 유감을 표명하지 않을 수 없다”고 국민의힘을 비판했다. 송 원내대표의 ‘일사부재의 원칙 위반 주장’에 대해 국회의장실 쪽은 전날 상정된 개헌안은 의결정족수(재적의원 3분의 2 찬성) 미달로 투표가 성립되지 않은 것으로 재투표를 하는 것은 문제 없다는 입장이다.)

Floor Leader Song directed his remarks at President Lee Jae-myung, Speaker Woo Won-shik, and the Democratic Party, saying, "Is the Constitution a toy for the Democratic Party, to be observed when they like it, violated when they don't, and smashed when they dislike it? Did they have any genuine intention to amend the Constitution? Or perhaps they needed a record of the PPP opposing the amendment when it was pushed through unilaterally without bipartisan agreement? Was there an ulterior motive to frame us as a party defending martial law, in order to gain the upper hand in local elections?" placing the blame for the failed passage of the constitutional amendment on them. (송 원내대표는 이재명 대통령, 우원식 국회의장과 더불어민주당을 향해 “맘에 들면 지키고 들지 않으면 어기고 맘에 안 들면 때려 부수는 헌법이 민주당의 장난감이냐”며 “개헌 의지가 있었냐. 혹시 개헌안을 여야 합의 없이 강행하면서 국민의힘이 반대했다는 기록이 필요했던 것 아니냐. 계엄 옹호 정당이라는 고약한 프레임 뒤집어씌워서 지방선거에서 유리한 고지를 점하려는 저의가 있었던 것 아니냐”고 개헌안 처리 무산의 책임을 돌렸다.)

Floor Leader Song said, "We are not fundamentally opposed to including events like the Busan-Masan Uprising and the May 18 Democratic Uprising in the preamble of the Constitution." He added, "The content of the Constitution's preamble should not focus on specific incidents but must be balanced under an integrated historical perspective. It should include the founding of the nation, and also incorporate the Saemaul Movement and modernization-related matters." (송 원내대표는 “부마항쟁, 5·18민주화운동 등을 헌법 전문 수록에 담는 데 대해 근본적으로 반대하지 않는다”며 “헌법 전문 내용은 특정 사건에 대한 것이 아니라 통합적 역사 인식 아래 균형 잡혀야 한다. 건국과 관련해 헌법에 넣어야 하고 새마을운동, 근대화 관련해서도 다 헌법에 포함해야 한다”고 했다.)

Furthermore, Floor Leader Song stated, "A constitutional amendment requires consensus between the ruling and opposition parties," and noted, "Historically, there have been cases where constitutional amendments were pushed through unilaterally, ignoring opposition party objections—such as the 'Sasao-ip Constitution' and the 'Yushin Constitution.'" He concluded, "They all ended in dictatorship and misfortune." (아울러 송 원내대표는 “개헌은 여야 합의가 필수”라며 “역사상 여야 합의 없이 일방적으로 야당 반대를 묵살하고 강행했던 개헌 사례가 있다. 사사오입 개헌, 유신헌법 개헌”이라며 “결말은 모두 독재와 불행으로 점철됐다”고 했다.)

Regarding Speaker Woo Won-shik's criticism of the PPP for boycotting the plenary session after suspending the voting process on the constitutional amendment, Chief Deputy Spokesperson Choi Soo-jin said, "It is regrettable that he speaks like a Democratic Party spokesperson," calling it "too emotional and biased." (최수진 원내수석대변인은 이날 우원식 국회의장이 헌법 개정안 표결 절차를 중단하며 본회의에 불참한 국민의힘을 비판한 데 대해 “민주당 대변인처럼 말해 유감”이라며 “너무 감정적이고 편파적인 말”이라고 말했다.)

Reporter Kim Hae-jeong sea@hani.co.kr (김해정 기자 sea@hani.co.kr)

item.title: Anti-Corruption Commission: "Jung Seung-yoon's Unjust Intervention Confirmed in Full Investigation of Lee Jae-myung's Helicopter Transfer" (권익위 “이재명 헬기 전원 조사, 정승윤 전 부위원장 부당 개입 확인”)
item.description:
The Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission (ACRC) announced on the 8th that it confirmed improper intervention by former ACRC Vice Chairman and Secretary General Jung Seung-yoon in the process of handling President Lee Jae-myung's "helicopter transfer report case" in 2024. At the time, Lee was the leader of the Democratic Party of Korea. The ACRC had concluded that Busan Fire Department officials and others violated the "Code of Conduct for Public Officials" in the use of a 119 emergency medical helicopter following the attack on President Lee, and Jung's intervention was involved in this process. <<> ACRC Chairperson Jeong Il-yeon said during a briefing on the results of the "ACRC Normalization Task Force (TF)" operation that day: "In the case of the report on violations of the Code of Conduct related to the 119 emergency helicopter, the former Secretary General (former Vice Chairman Jung Seung-yoon) had matters not discussed in the plenary committee agenda and meetings included in the resolution, and we also confirmed that he ordered notification of violations contrary to the opinion sent to the responsible department." The TF explained that while the responsible department at the time had issued an opinion for "institutional referral" with the intent of systemic improvement regarding the Busan Fire Department officials who decided to transfer President Lee via the 119 emergency medical helicopter, former Vice Chairman Jung ordered it to be handled as a "notified violation of the Code of Conduct." <<> President Lee, when he was the leader of the Democratic Party, was attacked with a knife on January 2, 2024, during a visit to Gadeokdo, Busan. He was then transferred via 119 emergency medical helicopter from Pusan National University Hospital to Seoul National University Hospital, which sparked controversy over preferential treatment. The ACRC began an investigation on January 16 of the same year, stating that "multiple reports have been received requesting an investigation into whether there was any illicit solicitation or provision of preferential treatment" related to the helicopter transfer. In July of that year, the ACRC concluded that doctors at Pusan National University Hospital and Seoul National University Hospital, as well as Busan Fire and Disaster Headquarters officials, had "confirmed violations of the Code of Conduct for Public Officials." <<> The TF, which re-investigated this, stated that it secured statements finding that "the helicopter transfer between Seoul National University Hospital and Pusan National University Hospital was based on the 'results of official inter-hospital transfer consultations,' and the doctor at Pusan National University Hospital had the medical authority to request the helicopter transfer." The TF's judgment is that deeming these officials in violation of the Code of Conduct was "inappropriate." <<> The TF announced that it would "express regret (apologize) at the ACRC level and, through systemic improvements, minimize unjust interventions that impede fair case processing by specific individuals abusing their position or authority." <<> Meanwhile, regarding the TF's announcement that day, former Vice Chairman Jung issued a statement, arguing that there was no problem with the decision at the time, stating: "Using the helicopter itself or receiving treatment at Seoul National University Hospital does not mean it was preferential treatment. The issue is whether there were procedures different from those for ordinary citizens in the process of using the helicopter and receiving treatment at the hospital." <<> On the same day, the TF also announced that it had confirmed that former Vice Chairman Jung held a late-night unofficial meeting (lasting one hour) with former President Yoon Suk-yeol, who was the subject of an investigation into the "Kim Keon-hee luxury bag receipt case," at the Yongsan presidential residence before the case was closed. <<> In response, former Vice Chairman Jung stated: "To the claim that I met and discussed with the president at night over something not urgent, I can only let out a hollow laugh." He added, "The truth will always come to light. I will fight to the end to protect liberal democracy and the rule of law." Jung, a professor at Pusan National University's Law School, has declared his candidacy for the Busan Superintendent of Education election. <<> Reporter Lee Seung-joon gamja@hani.co.kr Reporter Kim Chae-woon cwk@hani.co.kr (국민권익위원회(권익위)가 2024년 당시 더불어민주당 대표였던 이재명 대통령의 ‘헬기 전원 신고 사건 처리 과정’에서 정승윤 전 권익위 부위원장 겸 사무처장의 부적절한 개입을 확인했다고 8일 밝혔다. 권익위는 이 대통령 피습 사건 뒤 119 응급의료헬기 이용과정에서 부산소방본부 직원 등이 ‘공무원 행동강령을 위반했다’고 결론을 내렸는데, 여기에 정 전 부위원장의 개입이 있었다는 것이다.)

item.title: No More Mothers and Newborns Sacrificed to 'Emergency Room Roulette'... Ruling Party and Government Pledge "Special Measures" (‘응급실 뺑뺑이’로 산모·신생아 희생 없게…당정 “특단 대책 마련”)
item.description:
In connection with a recent incident in Cheongju where a mother lost her fetus while searching for an emergency delivery hospital, the government and the Democratic Party have decided to gather expert opinions and devise special measures to resolve the so-called 'emergency room roulette' problem. (최근 청주에서 산모가 응급 분만 병원을 찾다 태아가 사망한 사고와 관련, 정부와 더불어민주당이 이른바 ‘응급실 뺑뺑이’ 문제 해결을 위해 전문가의 의견을 모아 특단의 대책을 마련하기로 했다.)

The 'Democratic Party Task Force (TF) for Improving Emergency Medical Care for Mothers and Newborns' held a government-party meeting with the Ministry of Health and Welfare at the National Assembly on the afternoon of the 8th and received a briefing from the government on measures to address the issue. TF leader Rep. Lee Soo-jin stated, "We will prepare special measures to ensure that high-risk mothers and newborns no longer tragically lose their lives due to being unable to find a hospital," adding, "The ruling party and government will closely consult and actively gather opinions from field experts." <<> Deputy Minister of Health and Welfare Lee Hyung-hoon said, "I offer my deepest condolences and sympathy for the incident involving the mother and fetus in Cheongju," and added, "Our country currently faces limitations in regional maternal and child medical response due to a shortage of obstetrics and neonatology personnel and a decline in delivery infrastructure. The government will approach this with an open attitude so that field experiences and suggestions can lead to policy changes." <<> On this day, the TF appointed experts in obstetrics and gynecology, pediatrics, and neonatal emergency medicine as advisory committee members. After the meeting, Rep. Lee stated, "Improvement measures were proposed, including strengthening patient transfer and inter-facility cooperation, improving the compensation system, and establishing a severity-based treatment system for high-risk mothers and newborns," and added, "We plan to conduct more in-depth discussions with experts to incorporate field opinions and create detailed measures." <<> Reporter Yoo Young-jae young@hani.co.kr (‘민주당 산모·신생아 응급진료체계 개선 태스크포스(TF)’는 8일 오후 국회에서 보건복지부와 당정회의를 열고 정부로부터 문제 개선 방안을 보고받았다. 티에프 단장인 이수진 의원은 “더 이상 고위험 산모·신생아가 병원을 찾지 못해 안타깝게 생명을 잃는 일이 없도록 특단의 대책을 마련하겠다”며 “당정이 긴밀히 협의하고 현장 전문가 의견을 적극 수렴할 것”이라고 말했다.)

item.title: Is Justice Minister Chung Seong-ho the ‘Bodyguard’ for the Prosecution? Or is the Ministry of Justice a Subsidiary of the Prosecution? [Nonsseol] (검찰 ‘호위무사’ 정성호? 법무부가 검찰 산하기관인가 [논썰])
item.description:
Hello, everyone. This is Lee Jae-seong from Nonsseol. (여러분 안녕하십니까? 논썰의 이재성입니다.)

The Seoul High Prosecutors' Office Task Force (TF) established to inspect and investigate allegations of coercion and fabricated statements during the Yoon Seok-yeol administration's prosecution of the ‘Ssangbangwool North Korea Remittance’ case—the so-called ‘salmon and soju party’ scandal—has reportedly concluded the allegations are true and submitted its findings to the Supreme Prosecutors' Office. <<> ‘Salmon and soju party’ confirmed as fact <<> How do you feel upon hearing this news? Relieved that the suffocating weight has been lifted? Reassured by an expected outcome? I find myself feeling more frustrated. <<> The Ministry of Justice ordered the Seoul High Prosecutors' Office to form the TF last September. Was this case so complex that it required eight months? Why did it complete its investigation only about ten days before the May 17 expiration of the statute of limitations (three years) for disciplinary action? <<> According to media reports, the Seoul High Prosecutors' Office's conclusions are based on four main pieces of evidence: ① Statements from prison inmates who said they "directly heard Lee Hwa-young, former Deputy Governor of Gyeonggi Province for Peace, talking about drinking alcohol." ② Physical evidence showing former Ssangbangwool Director Park Sang-woong purchased soju and water at a convenience store near the detention center using a corporate card. ③ A recorded phone call between attorney Seo Min-seok, who served as Lee Hwa-young's lawyer, and Prosecutor Park Sang-yong, which Seo made public. ④ Results from a polygraph test administered to Lee Hwa-young. <<> Moreover, when ordering the establishment of the TF, the Ministry of Justice provided the Seoul High Prosecutors' Office with investigative materials compiled through a special inspection of detention center personnel and others. I simply cannot understand why this took so long. <<> Deputy Chief Justice of Seoul High Prosecutors' Office Jung Yong-hwan (acting head of the High Prosecutors' Office), who has overseen this case since serving as the head of the inspection division at the same office, acknowledged at a parliamentary hearing on April 30 titled "Yoon Seok-yeol's Political Prosecution and Indictment Manipulation" that the ‘salmon and soju party’ allegations have been confirmed. <<> Rep. Lee Yong-woo (Democratic Party of Korea): Former Ssangbangwool Vice Chairman Bang Yong-chul tried to hand over documents he was carrying to a Ssangbangwool employee in Prosecutor Park Sang-yong's office without permission, prompting the correctional officers present here today to protest—to Prosecutor Park Sang-yong. Also, when Park Sang-yong allowed Park Sang-woong, Park Sang-min, and Kim Seong-tae from Ssangbangwool to visit with coffee and outside food, the correctional officers protested again. Additionally, he arranged for former prosecutor turned lawyer Cho Jae-yeon (who hadn't been appointed as a defense attorney) to visit Lee Hwa-young, which is known as an attempt at coercion. He also facilitated these visits by connecting them. And under the guise of being witnesses, Ssangbangwool employees Park Sang-woong and Park Sang-min met with Kim Seong-tae countless times. Witness Jung Yong-hwan, you've confirmed all of this now, correct? <<> Jung Yong-hwan, Deputy Chief Justice, Seoul High Prosecutors' Office (acting head): Ah, yes. <<> Lee Yong-woo: You've also confirmed that some correctional officers protested these matters? <<> Jung Yong-hwan: There are some parts confirmed through statements. <<> Lee Yong-woo: According to answers given, correctional officers witnessed these accomplices gathered together in Room 1315, known as the storage room, waiting at Prosecutor Park Sang-yong's office. Additionally, correctional officers stated that Prosecutor Park Sang-yong arranged these individual meetings. Witness Jung Yong-hwan, you've confirmed this, yes? <<> Jung Yong-hwan: Yes, it is confirmed through statements. <<> (April 30, National Assembly hearing on 'Yoon Seok-yeol's Political Prosecution and Indictment Manipulation') <<> All confirmed actions are illegal <<> Bringing in outside food, meetings with a lawyer from a high-ranking prosecutorial background who hadn't even been appointed as counsel, passing documents, and meetings among accomplices—all of these actions are illegal. Now that these facts have been confirmed, why isn't there an official announcement? The decision on disciplining Prosecutor Park Sang-yong and others now rests with the Supreme Prosecutors' Office disciplinary committee. The statute of limitations for discipline runs out in less than ten days—can they actually impose any punishment? <<> I understand Deputy Chief Justice Jung Yong-hwan's difficult position. In an organization like the Korean prosecution, where a heavyweight championship in "protecting one's own" would be a foregone conclusion, I know how hard it is to investigate fellow prosecutors. But this inspection and investigation by the Seoul High Prosecutors' Office lacks any momentum. Instead, it feels stifled, hesitant, and wavering. Isn't this why Prosecutor Park Sang-yong is running around so arrogantly? <<> Prosecutor Park Sang-yong believes the prosecution organization is on his side. In fact, during this parliamentary hearing, only a handful of prosecutors—like Kim Tae-hoon, Head of Daejeon High Prosecutors' Office, and Jung Yong-hwan—admitted to even some of the prosecution's illegal acts. The rest shamelessly denied the facts, excused clear wrongdoings they couldn't deny as mistakes, and deflected responsibility. This hearing has laid bare how easily prosecutors ignore the law and human rights, and how tightly-knit an interest group they are. <<> Prosecutor General Won Seok-ahn and Song Kyung-ho protect illegal acts <<> Rep. Jung Tae-ho (Democratic Party): You still believe the three-day detention of Mr. Nam Wook was without issue, right? Answer yes or no. You seem to think it fell within the bounds of the law. <<> Former Prosecutor General Lee Won-seok: Yes, it falls within the bounds of the law. The detention facility is a lawful holding facility under our statutes. <<> Jung Tae-ho: Do you know if there are regulations for the detention facility? When I asked the Ministry of Justice, they said such regulations don't even exist because there are no cases of people being detained for several days and nights like this. And apparently, this is a remnant of Japanese colonial rule. When I asked for the regulations, they said there were none. <<> (April 21, National Assembly hearing on 'Yoon Seok-yeol's Political Prosecution and Indictment Manipulation') <<> They argue that confining a detained defendant (Nam Wook) in the prosecution's own detention facility instead of returning him to the prison is not illegal. While claiming ignorance of the specific details, they openly say they trust their own colleague. Look at how former head of Seoul Central District Prosecutors' Office Song Kyung-ho responded when questioned about Prosecutor Jeong Il-kwon, who allegedly threatened Nam Wook by saying "I'll slash your stomach" and showed him family photos to coerce and intimidate him during his three-day confinement. <<> Seo Young-kyo, Chair of the Special Committee on Parliamentary Investigation: Did witness Jeong Il-kwon make such remarks to witness Nam Wook or not? <<> Song Kyung-ho, former head of Seoul Central District Prosecutors' Office: I don't know the specific details but... <<> Seo Young-kyo: So, you don't know. Yes or no? <<> Song Kyung-ho: Based on the character and competence of Prosecutor Jeong Il-kwon that I experienced while working with him, I trust his explanation and position 100%. <<> Seo Young-kyo: That means you're wrong. Look at this—even when things are obvious, you protect your own. The whole nation knows it's wrong, yet you say you 100% trust him based on his character. This is exactly why witness Song Kyung-ho has been criticized for acting as a 'hunter.' Do you understand? <<> (May 1, National Assembly hearing on 'Yoon Seok-yeol's Political Prosecution and Indictment Manipulation') <<> Beyond 'prosecutorial solidarity' to 'criminal solidarity' <<> Prosecutor Jeong Il-kwon explained the reason for showing the family photos as follows. <<> Prosecutor Jeong Il-kwon: At the time, I showed the photos to Mr. Nam Wook out of humanitarian and moral considerations, to encourage him to think only of himself and his family. I do not believe it was illegal. <<> (April 7, National Assembly hearing on 'Yoon Seok-yeol's Political Prosecution and Indictment Manipulation') <<> He forcibly brought a defendant from prison using an arrest warrant, confined him in the basement detention facility of the Seoul Central District Prosecutors' Office, and showed him pictures of his children while telling him to think carefully—and calls this "humanitarian and moral considerations." But where did he get those children's photos? Mustn't they have been obtained through a search of Nam Wook's mobile phone? Among the data collected through the search, anything unrelated to the case should have been deleted, but instead it was kept and used for coercion. This violates both the constitutional principle of warrant requirements and the Criminal Procedure Act. Yet you still trust his "character and competence"? At this point, isn't this beyond 'prosecutorial solidarity' to 'criminal solidarity'? <<> This parliamentary hearing has exposed the ugly face of the prosecution: Prosecutor Park Sang-yong, who refused to take an oath; Prosecutor Kang Baek-shin, who yelled at members of the National Assembly, representatives of the people; and former prosecutor Ho Seung-jin, who threatened lawmakers by asking what they planned to do later. <<> Prosecutors walk out en masse when trial turns unfavorable <<> There's another case where the prosecution confessed to being a 'criminal solidarity.' Remember the prosecutors who collectively walked out of the perjury trial of former Gyeonggi Province Deputy Governor Lee Hwa-young after protesting the court? After Lee raised the 'salmon and soju party' allegations in the National Assembly, the prosecution indicted him for perjury. On November 25 last year, when Criminal Division 11 of the Suwon District Court (Presiding Judge Song Byeong-hoon) only accepted six of the witnesses the prosecution had applied for, they filed a motion to disqualify the judge, claiming they "cannot accept unfair trial management," and walked out en masse. <<> These prosecutors must have intended from the start to obstruct the trial. This case was being tried as a citizen participation trial, yet they applied for 64 witnesses. With many jurors attending, time for deliberation is limited in such trials, and requesting so many witnesses virtually forced the court to dismiss most of them. <<> In particular, this happened right after the Ministry of Justice's fact-finding report on the 'salmon and soju party' allegations—which I mentioned earlier—was submitted to the court. When the Ministry's submission put the prosecution at a disadvantage in the trial, they must have intended to make the trial impossible by applying for a flood of witnesses and a motion to disqualify the judge. They put forward impossible demands and then, when rejected, threw a fit and walked out. If they had nothing to hide, why wouldn't they proceed with the trial normally? <<> At the very least, it has been revealed to the world that the official position of the Suwon District Prosecutors' Office at the time—stating that no outside food was brought in—was false. Yet no one has admitted the truth or apologized. Instead, Lee Hwa-young, who exposed the truth, was indicted for perjury and put on trial, and when the trial became unfavorable, the prosecution walked out collectively. <<> Acting Prosecutor General criticizes parliamentary hearing <<> Last month, the Supreme Prosecutors' Office disciplinary committee rejected a proposed disciplinary action against these prosecutors. In such cases, the acting Prosecutor General should independently decide to seek discipline. But Acting Prosecutor General Koo Ja-hyun remains silent. He also gave lukewarm answers during this parliamentary hearing, clearly deferring to the prosecutors. In particular, when news broke that a prosecutor who had refused to attend the hearing had attempted suicide, Koo suddenly issued a statement criticizing the hearing. <<> Acting Prosecutor General Koo Ja-hyun: News reports yesterday and today have covered unfortunate news about a prosecutor selected as a witness for this parliamentary investigation. As acting Prosecutor General, I received this news with a heavy heart. <<> During the first report to the institution on April 3, I expressed concerns about this parliamentary investigation targeting cases still on trial, and requested that prosecutors who handled the work in accordance with the law and principles be allowed to testify as minimally as necessary. However, in the subsequent process, many prosecutors and investigators were called to testify, facing insults or being denied proper opportunities to respond. <<> (April 17, Q&A with reporters on leaving the Supreme Prosecutors' Office in Seocho-dong, Seoul) <<> Minister Chung Seong-ho ignores the president's orders <<> Can someone so busy deferring to prosecutors initiate disciplinary action against those who walked out en masse? Isn't that unlikely? Then the Ministry of Justice should directly pursue discipline. Recent legal amendments allow the Ministry to discipline prosecutors directly. But Justice Minister Chung Seong-ho only says he will 'review' it, and similarly, nothing comes of it. <<> Rep. Park Ji-won (Democratic Party): As the minister responsible for directing and supervising the prosecution, you should give the orders first. I don't think it's right to come to the Legislation and Judiciary Committee and say, 'I'll look into it,' only after the president does it. <<> Minister of Justice Chung Seong-ho: Even before the president spoke, we were already taking necessary measures. <<> Park Ji-won: Necessary measures—what did you do when the prosecutors walked out, Minister? <<> Chung Seong-ho: From the outset, we ordered an immediate investigation to determine the facts. Because I was at the National Assembly all day today, I haven't yet received a direct report. <<> (November 26, 2025, National Assembly Legislation and Judiciary Committee) <<> This was five months ago. It happened on the day President Lee Jae-myung ordered an inspection and investigation into the prosecutors who walked out en masse. Even after the president's order, Minister Chung's response was at this level. In media interviews, he even said, "Stabilizing the prosecution organization is the priority." Is he ignoring the president's orders? And five months later, when the Supreme Prosecutors' Office disciplinary committee decided it couldn't impose punishment, Minister Chung still has his hands off. <<> Is the Ministry of Justice a subsidiary of the prosecution? <<> Recently, the Ministry of Justice's official YouTube channel, 'MoJ TV,' has been posting a series of videos promoting the need for prosecutors' supplementary investigative powers. They argue that without prosecutors conducting 'supplementary' investigations into cases sent by the police, they might have been handled with summary orders or failed to prevent further crimes. If previously the prosecution used to provide 'successful supplementary investigation' materials to a few media outlets for articles, now the Ministry of Justice is openly and officially taking the lead. The prosecution's media spin is already criticizable, but now even the Ministry of Justice is unilaterally representing the prosecution's position. Is the Ministry of Justice a subsidiary of the prosecution? Has the prosecution become the Ministry's master? <<> The Ministry's actions are surely decided by Minister Chung Seong-ho. The minister himself has joined the PR campaign. Last Thursday, two perpetrators in the death of the deceased director Kim Chang-min—who died unjustly after being attacked in a restaurant brawl—were arrested. Minister Chung posted on Facebook that day, praising the prosecution's investigation. <<> "It was the result of a supplementary investigation, which provided a second chance to re-examine the case and get closer to the truth." (May 4, Justice Minister Chung Seong-ho's Facebook post) <<> He claims that while the police-led investigation failed to secure arrest warrants twice, the prosecution obtained warrants by conducting supplementary investigations, including searching the perpetrators' homes for new evidence. But can the arrest of the perpetrators seven months after the incident be explained solely by the prosecution's supplementary investigation? Isn't it reasonable to believe that the persistent protests of the bereaved family and media coverage of the perpetrators' inappropriate behavior significantly increased social attention and influenced the court's change of judgment? Moreover, we must ask what role the prosecution played when the court twice rejected the arrest warrants requested by the police. If the police's initial investigation was inadequate, couldn't the prosecutor have exercised their power to 'demand' supplementary investigations? Didn't the prosecution, like the police, just stand idly by with the attitude 'the court rejected it, so what can we do,' only to belatedly launch a supplementary investigation when public outrage grew? And now they're boasting that it was all due to their supplementary investigation—is that normal? <<> Currently, the Lee Jae-myung administration's prosecution reform is in the second of three stages. Following the passage of the Government Organization Act abolishing the Prosecution Service (Stage 1) and the laws establishing the Indictment Agency and the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency (Stage 2), the revision of the Criminal Procedure Act to define prosecutors' investigative powers (Stage 3) is pending. These procedures are all reform discussions based on separating investigation and indictment. Yet the prosecution and Ministry of Justice are throwing a tantrum, refusing to give up prosecutors' investigative powers. <<> Moreover, under the party-government-presidential office agreement, the revision of the Criminal Procedure Act has been postponed until after the June local elections. President Lee instructed the party to deliberate. But the Ministry of Justice has jumped ahead, setting conclusions and shaping public opinion before the Office of the Prime Minister even issues a government-wide position. Is this normal? <<> Supreme Prosecutors' Office refuses to uncover the truth about the insurrection <<> Do you know that Special Counsel Kwon Chang-young recently requested the Ministry of Justice to discipline Acting Prosecutor General Koo Ja-hyun and Inspection Chief Kim Seong-dong? The special counsel had requested documents from the Supreme Prosecutors' Office regarding the December 3 martial law declaration, but the office refused. The special counsel asked for materials investigated by the 'Prosecution Service's Constitutional Respect Government Innovation TF,' which the office had established itself to address the insurrection. But the office replied that the materials were "subject to non-disclosure under relevant regulations" and told the special counsel to obtain a search warrant if needed. The Special Counsel Act stipulates that the special counsel can request cooperation, including document requests, from relevant agencies (Article 6, Paragraph 3), and these agencies must comply. It also explicitly grants the power to request disciplinary proceedings in case of non-compliance (Article 6, Paragraph 6). <<> But regulations aren't the point here. The key fact is that Acting Prosecutor General Koo Ja-hyun 'refused' the special counsel's cooperation request. If he had any intention of addressing the insurrection, there would be no reason to refuse cooperation. This should be seen as stating that protecting the prosecution organization is more important than the national task of uncovering the truth. Will Minister Chung Seong-ho accept the special counsel's request and discipline Koo Ja-hyun? I doubt it. <<> Even after the people suppressed the insurrection and the regime changed, the prosecution remains unchanged. Isn't it an incorrigible group beyond repair? And the minister, who should control and correct the prosecution, remains under its sway, unable to regain his senses. <<> This has been Nonsseol. <<> Planning and Appearance: Editorial Writer Lee Jae-seong san@hani.co.kr <<> Direction and Editing: Producer Cho So-young (윤석열 정부 검찰의 ‘쌍방울 대북송금’ 사건 수사 과정에서 회유와 진술 조작이 있었다는 의혹이죠, 이른바 ‘연어술파티’ 의혹이 사실로 확인됐다고 이 사건을 감찰·수사해온 서울고검 인권침해점검 태스크포스(TF)가 결론 내렸습니다. 최근 대검찰청에 결과를 보고했다고 합니다.)

item.title: Defense Minister Ahn Kyu-baek to Make First U.S. Visit on the 10th, Expected to Discuss Wartime Operational Control and Nuclear Submarines (안규백 국방장관, 10일 첫 방미…전작권·핵잠수함 논의 전망)
item.description:
Defense Minister Ahn Kyu-baek plans to visit the United States for meetings with high-ranking officials to discuss various pending issues, including the transfer of wartime operational control (OPCON). (안규백 국방부 장관이 전시작전통제권(전작권) 전환 등 여러 현안을 논의하고자 미국을 방문해 고위급 인사들과 회담을 갖기로 했다.)

The Ministry of National Defense announced on the 9th that Minister Ahn will visit the United States from the 10th to the 14th. This marks his first trip to the U.S. since taking office in July last year. A defense ministry official stated regarding the visit, "It aims to facilitate direct high-level communication to follow up on the implementation of agreements from the South Korea-U.S. summit and the Security Consultative Meeting (SCM)," adding, "Wartime operational control and nuclear-powered submarines are expected to be major agenda items for discussion." (국방부는 9일 안 장관이 오는 10일부터 14일까지 미국을 방문한다고 밝혔다. 지난해 7월 취임한 뒤 첫번째 미국행이다. 국방부 관계자는 이번 방미를 놓고 “한미정상회담, 한미안보협의회(SCM) 합의사항 후속조치 관련 이행 점검차 고위급 간 직접 소통하려는 것”이라며 “전작권, 핵추진잠수함 등이 주요 현안으로 논의될 것”이라고 말했다.)

On the 11th (local time), Minister Ahn will hold a meeting with U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth in Washington, D.C. He is also scheduled to meet sequentially with high-ranking officials from the U.S. government and Congress, including the Acting Secretary of the Navy, the Chairman and Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, and the Chairman of the Seapower Subcommittee. (안 장관은 11일(현지시각) 미국 워싱턴 디시(D.C.)에서 피트 헤그세스 미국 국방부 장관과 회담을 하고, 미국 해군성장관 대행, 상원 군사위원장 및 간사, 해양력소위원장 등 미국 정부와 의회 고위급 인사를 차례로 만날 예정이다.)

Minister Ahn's visit to the U.S. comes amid a buildup of sensitive issues, such as the recovery of wartime operational control, cooperation on building nuclear-powered submarines, U.S. restrictions on sharing satellite information regarding North Korea, and demands for South Korea's contribution to the Strait of Hormuz. It is noteworthy whether this will become a turning point for pending matters in the South Korea-U.S. alliance. (안 장관의 방미는 전작권 회수와 핵추진잠수함 건조 협력, 미국의 대북 위성정보 공유 제한과 호르무즈 해협 기여 요구 등 민감한 사안이 쌓인 가운데 이뤄져 한미 동맹 현안의 변곡점이 될지 주목된다.)

The Lee Jae-myung administration is establishing a roadmap to achieve the transfer of wartime operational control by 2028, but a difference in perception has recently emerged as U.S. Forces Korea Commander General Xavier Brunson mentioned the first quarter of 2029 as a target timeline during a congressional hearing. (이재명 정부는 2028년에 전작권 전환이 이뤄질 수 있도록 로드맵을 마련하고 있지만, 최근 제이비어 브런슨 주한미군사령관이 의회 청문회에서 2029년 1분기를 목표 시점으로 언급하며 인식차가 드러났다.)

Additionally, follow-up procedures for cooperation in building nuclear-powered submarines, agreed upon by the South Korean and U.S. leaders in a joint statement last year, have not accelerated. During his visit to the U.S., Minister Ahn plans to meet with the Acting Secretary of the Navy to continue related discussions. Recently, the United States has demanded various military and non-military contributions from South Korea to resume navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, placing the South Korean government in a difficult position. (아울러 한미 정상이 지난해 공동 설명자료에서 합의한 핵추진잠수함 건조 협력의 후속 절차도 속도를 내지 못하고 있다. 안 장관은 방미 중 미국 해군성 장관 대행을 만나 관련 논의를 이어갈 예정이다. 최근 미국은 호르무즈 해협 통항 재개를 위해 한국의 각종 군사·비군사적 기여를 요구하고 있어 정부로서는 난감한 상황이다.)

South Korea and the U.S. will hold the Korea-U.S. Integrated Defense Dialogue (KIDD), a meeting body at the deputy assistant secretary level within defense authorities, from the 12th to the 13th in Washington, D.C., coinciding with Minister Ahn's visit. This meeting is expected to address overall security issues between the allies, including wartime operational control. Minister Ahn's visit this time is interpreted as a move to proactively find a breakthrough through preemptive high-level communication. (한미는 안 장관 방미 기간과 맞물리는 12일부터 13일까지 미국 워싱턴 디시(D.C.)에서 국방 당국 차관보급 회의체인 ‘통합국방협의체’(KIDD) 회의를 연다. 이 회의에서는 전작권 등 동맹국 간 안보 현안 전반이 논의될 예정인데, 안 장관의 이번 방미는 사전 고위급 소통을 통해 선제적으로 돌파구를 마련하려는 행보로 풀이된다.)

Reporter Jang Pil-soo feel@hani.co.kr (장필수 기자 feel@hani.co.kr)

item.title: Hong Jun-pyo: "Han Dong-hoon Recruits Torture-Affiliated Prosecutor and Preaches 'Kim Dae-jung's Spirit'...Lowbrow and Crude" (홍준표 “한동훈, 고문 검사 영입하고 ‘김대중 정신’…저급하고 조잡”)
item.description:
Former Daegu Mayor Hong Jun-pyo criticized former People Power Party leader Han Dong-hoon's candidacy in the Buk-gu Gap by-election in Busan, calling it "lowbrow and crude." (홍준표 전 대구시장이 한동훈 전 국민의힘 대표의 부산 북구갑 보궐선거 출마를 놓고 “저급하고 조잡하다”고 비난했다.)

On the 9th, Hong posted on Facebook about Han's recruitment of former lawmaker Chung Hyung-geun as his campaign committee chairman, stating, "Seeing an outsider candidate, who brings in a former prosecutor with a history of torture allegations as campaign chairman while inexplicably invoking Kim Dae-jung's spirit, it's hard not to feel that the election is devolving into something lowbrow and crude." (홍 전 시장은 9일 페이스북에서 한 전 대표가 정형근 전 의원을 후원회장으로 영입한 상황을 놓고 “고문 혐의 검사 출신을 (후원회장으로) 영입하면서 뜬금없이 김대중 정신을 외치는 외지인 후보를 보면서 참 선거가 저급하고 조잡하게 흐른다는 느낌을 배제하기 어렵다”고 꼬집었다.)

Hong also evaluated the Democratic Party's situation, which sparked controversy over "prosecutorial dismissal" ahead of local elections, as "a blunder stemming from immature political judgment." He pointed out, "The dismissal of an indictment is a system used by prosecutors before the first trial verdict when the real culprit is caught or when it becomes clear that the indictment was obviously wrong. Discussions on dismissing the indictment could have happened after the local elections." <<> He further explained, "In the case of political figures, there was an instance during the YS (Kim Young-sam) administration when the indictment for special tax evasion charges against POSCO Chairman Park Tae-joon was dismissed under Cheong Wa Dae's order. It wasn't dismissed because he was innocent, but as a political measure for grand unity," adding, "To handle President Lee Jae-myung's case similarly, appropriate political and judicial conditions must be in place." (홍 전 시장은 또 민주당이 지방선거를 앞두고 ‘공소취소’ 논란을 일으킨 상황을 놓고선 “정무적 판단 미숙으로 보이는 실책”이라고 평가했다. 홍 전 시장은 “공소취소 제도는 진범이 잡혔거나 기소 후 명백히 잘못된 기소로 밝혀질 때 검사가 1심 판결 전에 하는 제도”라며 “공소취소 논의는 지선이 끝난 후 해도 될 일”이라고 지적했다.)

Reporter Jang Pil-soo feel@hani.co.kr (그러면서 “정치인 관련 공소취소는 YS(김영삼) 정권 시절에 박태준 포스코 회장에 대한 특가법상 조세포탈 사건을 청와대의 지시로 공소 취소한 일이 있었다. 무죄라서 공소 취소한 것이 아니라 정치적 대화합 조치로 공소취소를 한 것”이라고 설명한 뒤 “이재명 대통령 사건을 이에 준하게 처리하려면 합당한 정치적, 사법적 환경이 전제되어야 할 것”이라고 덧붙였다.)

item.title: People Power Party Launches 'Indictment Cancellation Countermeasure TF' Vowing to "Inform Conservatives and Moderates of Its Injustice" (공소취소 대응 TF 띄운다는 국힘 “보수·중도층에 부당함 알릴 것”)
item.description:
The People Power Party (PPP) has decided to launch a 'Indictment Cancellation Countermeasure Task Force (TF)' to block the 'Special Counsel Act on Suspicions of Manipulated Investigations and Indictments by the Yoon Suk Yeol Administration' being pushed by the Democratic Party of Korea. (국민의힘이 더불어민주당이 추진하는 ‘윤석열 정권 조작 수사·기소 의혹 특검법’을 저지하기 위한 ‘공소취소 대응 태스크포스(TF)’를 출범시키기로 했다.)

PPP Senior Spokesperson Park Sung-hoon told reporters at the National Assembly on the 9th, "Once the Central Election Countermeasures Committee is launched next week, we will establish an 'Indictment Cancellation Countermeasure TF' as an internal body within the Central Election Countermeasures Committee." (박성훈 국민의힘 수석대변인은 9일 국회에서 기자들과 만나 “다음 주 중앙선거대책위원회를 출범하게 되면 중앙선대위 내부 기구 형태로 ‘공소취소 대응 TF’를 발족시킬 것”이라고 밝혔다.)

Park emphasized, "It is important to inform conservatives, centrists, and non-partisan voters how unjust the Indictment Cancellation Special Counsel Act is and how it violates the constitutional order of the Republic of Korea," adding, "We will find various effective ways to appeal to them." (박 대변인은 “보수층과 중도·무당층에도 공소취소 특검법이 얼마나 부당하고 대한민국 헌정 질서를 유린하는 행태인지 알리는 게 중요하다”며 “효과적으로 소구할 다양한 방안을 찾겠다”고 했다.)

The PPP plans to complete its candidate nominations for local government heads and by-elections for the local elections after selecting a candidate for the by-election of National Assembly members in Gongju, Buyeo, and Cheongyang in South Chungcheong Province on the 13th. Following that, the Central Election Countermeasures Committee will be launched, and according to convention, Representative Jang Dong-hyuk is expected to join as a co-chair of the committee. (국민의힘은 오는 13일 충남 공주·부여·청양 국회의원 보궐선거 후보 선출을 끝으로 지방선거 광역단체장·재보궐선거 공천을 마친다. 그 뒤 중앙선대위를 띄우고 관례대로 장동혁 대표가 공동선대위원장으로 합류할 전망이다.)

Meanwhile, regarding Representative Jang’s remarks at a foreign press briefing on the 8th, where he said, "One could assign a different political meaning to martial law," Park responded, "The PPP's final and official position is that the party declared a break from Yoon (severing ties with former President Yoon Suk Yeol) in the name of the entire party." (한편, 박 대변인은 지난 8일 장 대표가 외신기자 간담회에서 ‘계엄에 대해 다른 정치적 의미를 부여할 수도 있을 것’이라고 발언한 것을 두고는 “당 전원 명의로 절윤(윤석열 전 대통령과의 절연)을 선언한 것이 국민의힘의 최종적이고 공식적인 입장”이라고 답했다.)

On the situation where the opening ceremonies for PPP candidate Park Min-shik and independent candidate Han Dong-hoon in Busan's Buk-gu district are scheduled to take place simultaneously on the 10th, Park stated, "What matters now is not conservatives splitting and conflicting, but fighting against the Lee Jae-myung government as a united front," adding, "Please understand the urgent positions of the candidates who are running." (또 10일 부산 북구갑에서 박민식 국민의힘 후보와 한동훈 무소속 후보의 개소식이 동시에 열리는 상황을 놓고선 “지금 중요한 건 보수가 분열하고 갈등하는 모습이 아니라 단일대오로 이재명 정부와 싸우는 것”이라며 “절박한 심정으로 뛰는 후보들의 입장에서 판단해 줄 것”이라고 말했다．)
